manifest.criteria: Primary metric: per-seed mean validation MSE over the unseen budgets (37.5%, 75%). benefit iff the paired-bootstrap 95% CI of (conditioned - control) lies below 0, harm iff it lies above 0, insufficient-data when fewer than 5 paired seeds, otherwise no-benefit. Success iff benefit against both independent and pruned controls and the full-size (100%) validation MSE against pruned is not harm. Per-budget comparisons are exploratory.
manifest.criteriaBudgetInput: Second hypothesis, declared on 2026-11-16 before the budgetInput arm's first run: the same rule as CRITERIA applied to budgetInput in place of conditioned (benefit against both independent and pruned on the unseen-budget mean, and full-size validation MSE against pruned not harm). budgetInput minus conditioned on the unseen-budget mean is exploratory.

paper.title: Learning Time-Varying Connectomes for Stable Behavior Across Development
paper.readVia: search-indexed excerpts of https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06895 and https://arxiv.org/html/2611.06895; direct fetch refused by the host proxy

elements.paper: One compact generative encoding: a HyperNEAT CPPN that takes developmental time as an extra input and emits age-specific connectivity for a recurrent controller.
elements.study: conditioned arm: one genome of weights, biases and an evolved expression-priority gene; a budget keeps the top-k candidate synapses by priority. The genome has no budget input.

elements.paper: Developmental time (T) is an input to the generator, so connectivity and weights can change with age rather than only grow or shrink.
elements.study: budgetInput arm: each candidate synapse carries a priority and a weight that are linear in the budget (priority + slope × budget, weight + slope × budget), so the budget is an input to expression and the kept set need not be nested across budgets. A linear rule per synapse, not a CPPN over coordinates.

elements.paper: The substrate (neuron birth, position, sensory organisation, intrinsic time constants) is prescribed per age; only connectivity is generated.
elements.study: One fixed candidate topology (4 inputs, 8 hidden, 1 output, 44 candidate synapses); the budget sets how many candidates are expressed.

elements.paper: Developmentally aware conditions optimise mean fitness across 3, 5 or 15 evenly spaced developmental snapshots.
elements.study: The conditioned arm optimises mean calibration MSE across 3 budgets: 25%, 50% and 100% (not evenly spaced).

elements.paper: Performance is measured over the whole developmental interval, at trained and at unseen ages, on 20 test trials whose starting states and stimulus sequences were not seen during optimisation.
elements.study: Validation MSE at the trained budgets and at the unseen 37.5% and 75%, on a validation split no search reads.

elements.paper: In testing, the substrate's developmental age and the CPPN's time input are set separately; for developmentally aware controllers both are set to the testing age.
elements.study: budgetInput is expressed with its budget input equal to the evaluation budget, which also sets the synapse count; the study does not separate the two.

elements.paper: Controls: standard HyperNEAT optimised at the initial substrate only (T=0) and 'Reverse' HyperNEAT at the mature substrate only (T=1), with the CPPN time input held at its training value during testing (five conditions in all).
elements.study: Controls: independent per-budget searches (including the unseen budgets, which is stronger than single-snapshot training) and a full-size search pruned by frozen-weight magnitude, all at an equal charged-record budget.

elements.paper: Five independent evolutionary runs per condition for each substrate-task pair, populations of 100 genomes evolved for 200 generations.
elements.study: 20 seeds per arm, stopped by an equal charged-calibration-record budget rather than a generation count.

elements.paper: Two substrates (Fish, Ring) and two closed-loop visuomotor tasks (optomotor response, phototaxis).

Substrates are prescribed by a developmental interpolation g(T): Fish g(T)=T, recurrent cohort ranks assigned outside to inside; Ring g(T)=T², inside to outside; intrinsic time constants τ(T)=0.4−0.2T (Fish) and 0.4−0.2T² (Ring); substrate coordinates are used without normalisation.
elements.study: No developmental substrate: the candidate topology and the TANH/IDENTITY squashes are fixed; only the number and choice of expressed synapses varies.

unpinned: CPPN inputs beyond developmental time, its output activation and how connections are thresholded (the paper cites HyperNEAT-LEO; whether it uses a link-expression output was not confirmed)
the NEAT settings of the CPPN search beyond population size and generation count
the fitness definitions for the optomotor and phototaxis tasks
the values of the unseen ages (the excerpts say standard HyperNEAT was tested at three unseen developmental times, but not which)

manifest.ockham: Unlike NEAT-AI-Ockham's frozen-weight pruning, the expression order here is an evolved, heritable gene; the pruned control ranks a finished network's frozen weights by magnitude.

reasons: conditioned does not beat independent per-budget searches on unseen budgets (harm)
conditioned regresses against the pruned arm at the full-size budget
budgetInput does not beat independent per-budget searches on unseen budgets (harm)
budgetInput does not beat the magnitude-pruned full-size network on unseen budgets (no-benefit)
budgetInput regresses against the pruned arm at the full-size budget
